questions.prompt: What should come first when building a production prompt?

options.text: Defining measurable success criteria and building a test set

questions.explanation: Criteria and test sets drive every later decision, from architecture to the release gate.

questions.prompt: Which belong in a prompt card? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A prompt card documents what the prompt does, how it was tested, where it breaks, and how it changed. Secrets never belong in prompts or their docs.

questions.prompt: An automated check that blocks deployment when evaluation metrics miss their thresholds is called a release ____.
questions.explanation: A release gate enforces quality targets every time, for example by failing a CI pipeline.

questions.prompt: TicketTriage needs refund policies the model doesn't know and must validate the classification before drafting. Which architecture fits?

options.text: A single prompt with no extra knowledge
A two-step chain (classify, then draft) with policy retrieval and one read-only tool
A fully autonomous agent with permission to send emails
Fine-tuning a new model from scratch

questions.explanation: Knowledge needs suggest retrieval, the checkpoint suggests a chain, and the only action (order lookup) needs a read-only tool. No send permission keeps humans in control.

items.text: Define the job and success criteria
Ship with a release gate and monitoring
Evaluate and iterate one change at a time

questions.explanation: Define, choose the architecture, build and iterate with evaluation, secure, then ship with a gate and keep monitoring.

questions.prompt: Match each production practice to its purpose.

pairs.right: Lets anyone understand and safely change the prompt
A free, honest signal of draft quality
Re-testing before a model or API change

questions.explanation: Each practice keeps a production prompt trustworthy over time, not just on launch day.
